skill.name: threejs-loaders
skill.description: Use Three.js loaders to import 3D models, textures, and environment maps. Configure glTF compression, report progress, and manage asset cleanup in WebGL and WebGPU applications.
skill.summary: Load, configure, and dispose of Three.js assets in browser scenes.
skill.author: cloudai-x

security_audit.summary: All 94 static alerts are false positives involving Markdown, JavaScript strings, ordinary asset requests, or geometry attribute enumeration. Two examples lack safeguards for untrusted asset references and failed Blob URL cleanup. No evidence of prompt injection, credential access, or intentional data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: The file-input parsing example does not restrict secondary asset URLs.
remediation.suggestion: For untrusted imports, reject external resource references before parsing. If external assets are required, enforce an explicit origin allowlist and browser request policy.

remediation.issue: The texture helper leaves the Blob URL active when loading fails.
remediation.suggestion: Revoke the Blob URL in a finally block so cleanup runs whether the texture loads or fails.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Models Can Reference External Assets
semantic_findings.description: The guide suggests parsing files from a file input without limiting the model's resource URLs. An untrusted glTF can trigger additional browser requests for referenced textures or buffers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide recommends the same parsing method for file-input bytes, and the path example shows that model references resolve separately. Browser policy determines which requests can proceed.

semantic_findings.title: Failed Texture Loads Retain Blob URLs
semantic_findings.description: The helper revokes its Blob URL only after the texture loads successfully. Repeated failures with large input files can retain browser memory while the page remains open.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: If loadAsync rejects, execution skips the revocation line. The browser can retain the underlying Blob until revocation or document unload.

content.user_title: Load Models and Textures in Three.js
content.value_statement: Three.js assets can fail to load or render incorrectly when their loader, decoder, or color space does not match the file. This guide shows how to pick loaders, report progress, and release resources when a scene changes.
actual_capabilities: Load glTF and GLB scenes and play their animation clips.
Configure Draco and meshopt geometry decoding and KTX2 texture support for glTF.
Choose loaders for OBJ with MTL, FBX, STL, PLY, and USD assets.
Set texture color spaces and map HDR, EXR, or UltraHDR images for scene lighting.
Report progress across several loaders, cancel supported requests, and configure the shared asset cache.
Clone skinned models for independent animation and dispose of geometry, materials, and textures.
limitations: Examples target Three.js r186. Imports and renderer methods can differ in older releases.
The guide shows how to load compressed assets. It does not compress or convert source files.
TextureLoader does not report image download progress and does not honor LoadingManager cancellation.
The file-input example does not validate untrusted assets or restrict their external resource references.

prompt_templates.title: Load a first GLB
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Add a local model to an existing WebGL scene.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to load my local GLB with GLTFLoader and add it to my scene. Include lighting and explain how to report a load failure.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a washed-out texture
prompt_templates.scenario: Developing: A replacement color texture looks different from the original.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the color space and vertical orientation of the replacement color and normal maps on my glTF model. Explain which settings differ between the maps.

prompt_templates.title: Configure compressed assets
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: A project loads several compressed assets and needs progress reporting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the glTF extensions I provide to choose Draco, meshopt, or KTX2 support. Show a shared loading manager and explain which requests it can cancel.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a WebGPU model swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: A viewer replaces animated characters without reloading the page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a WebGPU model swap with renderer initialization, KTX2 support detection, and independent animation for each clone. Describe when to dispose of shared resources.

output_examples.input: My GLB loads, but the model looks black. I have an HDR image.
output: Load the HDR image and set its mapping to equirectangular reflection.
Assign the texture to the scene environment so it lights the model.
Set the scene background separately when you also want to show the image behind the model.

output_examples.input: How do I show progress while loading a model and two textures?
output: Share one loading manager between the model and texture loaders.
Report completed items out of the total instead of estimating image download percentages.
Handle rejected asset promises separately from the progress display.

output_examples.input: My cloned characters all follow the original animation. How can I play different clips?
output: Clone the model with SkeletonUtils so each copy has its own bones.
Create a separate animation mixer for each character.
Keep shared geometry and materials until no character uses them.

best_practices: Match self-hosted decoder and transcoder files to the Three.js release used by your application.
Set sRGB on color textures and leave data maps, such as normal and roughness maps, without a color space.
Track resource ownership so you release geometry, materials, and textures only after their last use.
anti_patterns: Calling KTX2 support detection before WebGPURenderer finishes initialization.
Using Object3D.clone when each skinned character needs independent bones.
Assuming removing a model from the scene releases its GPU resources.

faq.question: Which Three.js release does this guide target?
faq.answer: The examples target Three.js r186 and include both WebGL and WebGPU renderer setups.

faq.question: Which model formats are covered?
faq.answer: The guide covers glTF, GLB, OBJ with MTL, FBX, STL, PLY, and USD variants.

faq.question: Do all glTF files require a decoder?
faq.answer: No. Configure Draco or meshopt when the model requires that geometry compression. Add KTX2 support when the model uses KTX2 textures.

faq.question: Can I cancel every load with LoadingManager?
faq.answer: No. The manager can cancel supported FileLoader requests, but it does not cancel image-element requests from TextureLoader.

faq.question: Can I use an HDR image for lighting without displaying it?
faq.answer: Yes. Assign the mapped texture to the scene environment and leave the background unchanged.

faq.question: Does this guide validate models from uploads?
faq.answer: No. Validate untrusted files and restrict any external resource references before passing them to a loader.
